Final numeric tallies: Gershon has שְׁלֹשָֽׁה at oshb:1Chr.23.8 and אַרְבָּעָֽה at oshb:1Chr.23.10, but Kohath has אַרְבָּעָֽה at oshb:1Chr.23.12 and Merari שְׁלֹשָֽׁה at oshb:1Chr.23.23 — the same device, same position. primary_reviews.rationale: This is a candid repair - the false discriminator is withdrawn rather than patched, the counter-evidence is spelled out, both dispositions are put to the ruling body and confidence is held down - and I would not disturb that posture. primary_reviews.rationale: I set out to break this row's exclusivity claim and could not. Sweeping שרי הצבא across 1Chronicles returns 25:1, 26:26 and 27:3 — the two later hits fall outside 23:1-25:31, so the row's first-occurrence assertion holds exactly as bounded, and bounding it to the part rather than the book was the right call, since הצבא alone appears as early as 12:15. Both bracket quotations byte-match their verses, the numeral 288 is quoted correctly from v7, and v8's lot-casting formula does begin a differently shaped sub-unit. Two adjacent data are worth recording without disturbing the verdict. The collocation "וַיְהִ֨י מִסְפָּרָ֤ם" also stands at 23:3, so the v1/v7 frame is the Chronicler's standing muster idiom rather than a bespoke device — the row claims only that it brackets this roster, which it does. And the בדל root occurs three times in the book (12:9, 23:13, 25:1); the nearest antecedent, 23:13's niphal "וַיִּבָּדֵ֣ל אַהֲרֹ֡ן", contrasts in stem with the hiphil "וַיַּבְדֵּ֣ל" here, which would sharpen rather than weaken the row's contrast with division-and-lot vocabulary if it were cited.

The inclusio argument is textually earned: v1 opens 'וַֽיְהִי֙ מִסְפָּרָ֔ם' and v7 closes with the same two words before its own tally, giving this roster a front-to-back frame distinct from the lot-casting idiom that opens v8. The 'set apart' verb link back to 23:13's Aaronic consecration ('וַיִּבָּדֵ֣ל') is an accurate, non-trivial cross-reference rather than a stretch.

primary_reviews.rationale: The instinct to keep the twenty-four lots whole is right, and the count verifies: a consonantal tally of שנים עשר returns twenty-four occurrences across vv9-31 (25:19 carries it twice, once as its own ordinal), so the sequence is complete and closes only when the roll is exhausted. The v8 and v9 quotations are byte-exact, and the 24:7 comparandum carries the book's sole remaining instance of the ויצא הגורל opener (consonantal sweep). But the row does not merely keep the unit whole, it asserts perfect uniformity and the absence of any subgroup marker, and that is a universal claim the brief requires me to test mechanically. Tested, it fails: the ordinals split into two morphologically distinct halves at exactly the twelfth/thirteenth item, and the row's own quotation of v9 contradicts its no-verb assertion.

challenges.claim: The row states that "no textual marker separates any subgroup from the next -- every single item shares the identical ordinal-name-twelve pattern start to finish." A first-token test over vv9-31 falsifies this. Items one through twelve carry the ordinal bare or with the article and no preposition, ending at 25:19 "הַשְּׁנֵ֤ים עָשָׂר֙"; from 25:20 "לִשְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה עָשָׂר֙" through 25:31 "לְאַרְבָּעָ֤ה וְעֶשְׂרִים֙" every remaining ordinal carries a prefixed lamed, twelve verses in a row without exception. The shift falls precisely at the halfway point of a twenty-four item list and is visible in the translation as well (WEB turns to "for the thirteenth" at v20), so it is a textual marker, and the assertion that none exists is not sustainable as written.
challenges.suggested_action: Qualify the uniformity claim: state that the refrain's semantic shape is constant while its ordinal morphology shifts from bare/definite to lamed-prefixed at 25:19/20, and argue on the record why a prefix alternation of this kind is too weak to carry a tier-1 seam (it introduces no head, no subject, and no closure formula) rather than denying the alternation exists. So the pe at 26:5 punctuates the close of the Obed-Edom sub-list, which is also why it lands where the original item located it, at the v5/v6 turn into Shemaiah's generation. primary_reviews.rationale: Both language repairs land. Stripping pointing from oshb:1Chr.26.29 leaves ליצהרי כנניהו ובניו למלאכה החיצונה על ישראל לשטרים ולשפטים, where neither יהוה nor מלך appears, whereas 26:30 carries both and 26:32 sets האלהים beside המלך -- so the corrected description of what the bracket encloses is what the witness shows. The 26:23 gentilics are consonantally identical to the heads at v29 and vv30-31, as the row now says. Arithmetic holds: אלף ושבע מאות at v30 is 1,700 and אלפים ושבע מאות at v32 is 2,700. Two defects survive the rewrite, both in load-bearing places. The rationale's exclusivity claim fails a lexical intersection: v29 and v30 share על and ישראל as well as the מלאכה root, and עַל יִשְׂרָאֵה answered by עַ֚ל פְּקֻדַּ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל is a jurisdiction formula at least as strong as the root tie the row calls its only one. Separately, the single stated ground for keeping v29 in this row -- 26:20's governing head -- is neither quoted nor referenced, and the one WLC mark at this row's opening edge, the petuchah closing 26:28, is passed over while the petuchah at 26:32 is cited for the close. Every pointed Hebrew string in the row byte-matches the verse it is attributed to; the two unpointed forms are lemma citations, checked consonantally rather than as quotations.

challenges.claim: The rationale asserts that 'the only tie it carries forward is the shared root לַמְּלָאכָ֤ה ... answered by מְלֶאכֶת ... in v30'. A third tie is the one the row's own rejected alternative relies on -- both verses open with a lamed-plus-gentilic head drawn from the 26:23 list -- which the rationale's 'only' sentence silently contradicts.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace 'the only tie' with the actual inventory: the shared lamed-plus-gentilic register head, the על + ישראל jurisdiction formula, and the מלאכה/מלאכת root. The row's conclusion is strengthened, not weakened, by stating them.

Scanning oshb 26.29 word by word turns up neither the divine name nor the royal noun; both appear only in v30 (לְכֹל֙ מְלֶ֣אכֶת יְהוָ֔ה וְלַעֲבֹדַ֖ת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ) and v32 (לְכָל דְּבַ֥ר הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים וּדְבַ֥ר הַמֶּֽלֶךְ), so the bracket actually encloses vv30-32 and excludes the one verse the rejected_alternative built it to retain; the most that survives is a weaker root-level tie, לַמְּלָאכָ֤ה (v29) against מְלֶ֣אכֶת (v30). LF's independent catch targets the adjacent sentence: v31's fortieth-year search at Jazer of Gilead explains only v32's 2,700 (Jerijah's kin), not v30's 1,700 (Hashabiah's men, a separate notice carrying no search language) -- confirmed against both totals in oshb -- and v30/v31 both open on the identical repeated head לַֽחֶבְרוֹנִי, a possible internal seam the rejected_alternative never tests. OL's remaining, lower-severity point ties back into D131: v29's opening word resumes the same Izharite/Hebronite gentilic list introduced at 26.23 (cross-reference the D131 finding above on OL-M8-1Chr-131-2), so this row's own opening is a continuation of an already-running list rather than a fresh, unheralded topic. LF's v32 gloss catch is a clean citation-accuracy finding: 1Chr_web_clean.txt reads 'for every matter pertaining to God and for the affairs of the king,' not the row's more literal 'for every matter of God and matter of the king.' None of these four findings by itself relocates the span, but together they leave the row's 'high' confidence and its v29-attachment argument resting on weaker textual ground than stated -- a confidence/argument-adequacy question for the author/boss round, not a span change I am making here.

Every one of the twelve mark cites is correct against pmarks_1Chr.json — samekh at 27:1, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 and pe at 27:15, all single-witness, none doubled and none claimed to be. I record one presentational asymmetry without raising it to a challenge: v3 breaks the refrain on the same footing as v6, yet only v6 is explained.

This is the cluster's cleanest boundary call: the refrain, the samekh chain, and the strategy doc's explicit call to hold the twelve-fold course rotation together as one unit all point the same way, and folding the Benaiah aside (v6) into the row rather than re-heading at v7 is correct since v7 resumes the same captain-and-number pattern without any new formula. primary_reviews.rationale: The attribution defect is repaired and the marker reasoning survives checking. Every samekh the row lists for 27:1, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 is present in the marker profile, the pe at 27:15 is present, and none of the three unmarked verses in the run is claimed as marked -- so 'nearly every' is exact rather than generous. The refrain claim also verifies: the full formula וְעַל מַחֲלֻקְתּוֹ עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה אָלֶף stands twelve times across vv2-15, once per captain, with v1 carrying the header variant, giving thirteen occurrences of the number in the span. The Benaiah aside at v6 does break the closing formula and v7 does resume without a new head. What the repair did not do is check the gloss it now formally adopts. By writing that 'the first division, twenty-four thousand' is the author's own literal rendering, the row makes the accuracy of that rendering its own claim, and הָֽאַחַ֔ת is the attributive cardinal, not the ordinal -- which is why WEB reads it distributively and why the row's next sentence has to quote הָרִֽאשׁוֹנָה֙ from v2 for the actual first division. All pointed Hebrew in this row byte-matches its verse.

challenges.claim: The repair converts an unattributed English phrase into an asserted literal rendering of the Hebrew, and the rendering is wrong at the point that matters. In הַֽמַּחֲלֹ֨קֶת֙ הָֽאַחַ֔ת עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֖ה אָֽלֶף (oshb:1Chr.27.1) the numeral is the attributive cardinal אַחַת agreeing with a definite noun -- 'the one division', i.e. each single division -- which is why WEB generalises it as 'of every division were twenty-four thousand'. The ordinal 'first' renders הָרִֽאשׁוֹנָה֙, which the row itself quotes two sentences later from oshb:1Chr.27.2. So the gloss both misdescribes v1's numeral and collides with the row's own v2 citation, and it undercuts the argument it is offered for: only the distributive sense lets v1 'set the refrain quantity' that recurs after all twelve captains.
challenges.suggested_action: Re-gloss the phrase as 'the one division' or 'each single division: twenty-four thousand', reserving 'first' for הָרִֽאשׁוֹנָה֙ at v2, and keep the existing note that WEB smooths the clause.

The rejected alternative turns on calling v23's opening 'a continuing waw-form', but וְלֹא נָשָׂ֤א דָוִיד֙ is waw plus negative plus qatal, the standard non-continuing construction Hebrew uses to suspend a wayyiqtol chain for background comment -- the very thing the row elsewhere calls an inset. The conclusion survives restatement; the stated reason does not. I also note the row leaves the samekh at 27:24 undisclosed, which is the one mark bearing on its own terminal edge.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative rules out a row beginning at v23 because 'the clause opens with a continuing waw-form rather than a register-head formula'. WEB reflects this with 'But David didn't take the number of them'. The distinction is one this cluster elsewhere insists on: M8-1Chr-137 argues, correctly, that wayyiqtol is the continuing form. As stated, the reason is not merely imprecise but points the wrong way, since a disjunctive opening is if anything a mild signal in favour of the rival being rejected.

primary_reviews.rationale: Both cures are in place and are stated with the right force -- the pe is neutralised for the 27:31/32 question in the rejected alternative while still being offered, legitimately, as weak corroboration of the row's terminal edge at the chapter close, which is a different seam and not a contradiction. primary_reviews.rationale: Collation first: the whole of 28:1 as reproduced in the rationale, plus וַיָּ֨קָם דָּוִ֤יד הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ עַל רַגְלָ֔יו and שְׁמָע֖וּנִי אַחַ֣י וְעַמִּ֑י from 28:2, reproduce 1Chr_oshb.txt character for character, accents included. The morphological label is also right — וַיַּקְהֵ֣ל is the H-stem (hiphil) wayyiqtol of קהל, so 'hiphil summons' is an accurate description of the opening verb, and the catalogue does terminate at אֶל יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם with no further finite verb inside v1. Chapter 28 carries 21 verses in both witnesses (counted from 1Chr_web_clean.txt and 1Chr_oshb.txt), so this row sits outside the WEB/MT offset zones and no dual-cite obligation applies; every ref in the row resolves to an existing verse in the witness it names. What does not survive checking is the syntactic seal the row places between v1 and v2, argued below. I draw no inference from the fact that pmarks_1Chr.json keys no mark to 28:1: under the Writings policy absence of a mark is not counterevidence in either direction, and I have not used it as any.

challenges.claim: The row's load-bearing grammatical claim — that the roster is 'grammatically self-contained' with 'no verb chain carrying past that point,' and that 'v2's inquit does not extend v1's verb chain' — is not what the Hebrew shows. Verse 2 opens וַיָּ֨קָם דָּוִ֤יד הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ עַל רַגְלָ֔יו: a consecutive wayyiqtol, which is precisely the form that continues a preceding narrative chain, and the chain it continues is v1's וַיַּקְהֵ֣ל. Nothing severs it. Second, the imperative that follows, שְׁמָע֖וּנִי אַחַ֣י וְעַמִּ֑י, is 2mp and its vocative is a bare appellation ('my brothers and my people') that names no group on its own — the referent it depends on is the enumerated officer-classes gathered in v1, and no other candidate audience has been introduced. Verse 1 thus supplies the participant set v2's speech turns to address (tier-1: verb-chain syntax plus participant continuity). The observation that actually holds is narrower: v1 anticipates no quotation. That is a register-to-speech transition, not syntactic closure.
challenges.suggested_action: Re-argue the 1/2 seam on the register-to-speech-inauguration transition alone and delete the verb-chain-closure assertion; then either drop confidence from 'high' to medium, or have the mesh weigh the rival the row never states — 28:1 read as the participant-setting head of one convocation-and-address unit with 28:2-7 — on its merits.

primary_reviews.rationale: The hiphil gathering verb וַיַּקְהֵל opens a self-contained officer-catalogue that ends flush at 'to Jerusalem,' and the paired wayyiqtol of v2 (קם...ויאמר) launches an entirely new inquit with no verb chain reaching back into v1 -- the convocation-to-speech seam is textbook tier-1, matching the strategy's own device-matrix entry for 28:1 ויקהל.

This is a thorough repair and the replacement grounds survive testing. וַיַּקְהֵל is indeed hiphil, and my own sweep of אמר forms across 28:1-29:22 returns 28:2, 28:3, 28:6, 28:20, 29:1, 29:10 and 29:20 -- so v2 does carry the first inquit anywhere after the roster, and v1 opens no quotation frame, which is exactly the narrower ground the row now stands on. The vocative אַחַ֣י וְעַמִּ֑י names no group by itself, as claimed. The catalogue description matches the Hebrew class by class, including הַסָּרִיסִ֧ים for officers. One observation offered as support rather than objection: the roster recapitulates the registers just catalogued almost term for term -- המחלקות and המשרתים את המלך and ושרי האלפים against oshb:1Chr.27.1, and שרי כל רכוש ... למלך against שָׂרֵ֣י הָרְכ֔וּשׁ אֲשֶׁ֖ר לַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִֽיד at oshb:1Chr.27.31 -- which reinforces the row's participant-continuity reading. Minor and not filed: the parenthetical rendering of v2's opening omits דָוִיד, which stands in the Hebrew string being glossed. All pointed Hebrew here byte-matches its verse.

The grammar claim is now accurate: וַיָּקָם in v2 is conceded as a continuing wayyiqtol rather than a chain-breaking form, and the argument correctly narrows to the absence of any quotation frame in v1 plus the bare vocative in v2 whose referent depends on v1's roster. This is a materially weaker and more defensible claim than the original, matched by the confidence downgrade to medium. No fresh defect found.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: OL's grammatical catch is correct: v2 opens with a consecutive wayyiqtol (David stood up on his feet and said) that formally continues the same narrative chain v1's gathering verb (vayyaqhel, 'and he assembled') begins -- Hebrew wayyiqtol chains do not sever at unit boundaries, they run through them, so 137's 'no verb chain carrying past that point' and 'v2's inquit does not extend v1's verb chain' overclaim a syntactic seal that is not there. The salvageable ground is the narrower one OL names: v1's roster opens no direct-discourse frame, and the audience the imperative addresses ('hear me, my brothers and my people') is recoverable only from v1's own participant list -- a register-to-speech transition, not a chain break. That narrower ground gets independent, if non-authorizing, support from book_strategy_draft.md's device matrix, which lists 28:1's gathering wayyiqtol and 28:2's speech frame as two SEPARATE tier-1 devices. Whether 'high' confidence survives once the flawed sentence is removed is a real question the correction raises; that call belongs to the author/boss round, not this review.

One of two legs gone; confidence high→medium RATIFIED.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative disposes of a v4 break by saying 'no inquit reopens there.' That is true at v4 — and it is the one internal position where the row's own criterion cannot bite. A programmatic sweep of אמר forms over 28:1-29:22 returns 28:2, 28:3, 28:6, 28:20, 29:1, 29:10, 29:20; two of those (וְהָאֱלֹהִים֙ אָ֣מַר לִ֔י at 28:3, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לִ֔י at 28:6) fall inside this very span, and the second is a full wayyiqtol inquit introducing the divine quotation that runs to the end of v7. primary_reviews.rationale: David's address runs unbroken from the already-open v2 inquit through the embedded divine quotations of v3 and vv6-7, and the row correctly treats the temporal tag כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה as the point where the recited promise -- not the speech itself -- closes, so the seam falls at v7|v8 rather than at any of the internal quotation shifts.

The substituted rival is the right one and the criterion is now on the page. My independent sweep of אמר over 28:1-29:22 reproduces the same seven positions the challenge reported, confirming that 28:3 and 28:6 are the only speech frames inside this span and that they are first-person recollections nested in David's recital rather than narrator-level frames. The sweep this repair rests on reproduces exactly. Across 1 Chronicles חזק appears at fifteen verses and אמץ at six, and the intersection is precisely {22:13, 28:20}, so the two-verse figure is sound. 22:16 collates byte-exact and does furnish the do-imperative-plus-accompaniment pairing that 28:20's עִמָּ֔ךְ answers, which makes the repertoire reading substantive instead of a hedge dressed as an argument. The support-roster half of the decision is equally solid: the vav-prefixed with-you word opens 28:21 as quoted, the priest-and-Levite clause and the closing captains clause both collate, and the chapter-crossing inquit at 29:1 is verbatim in both witnesses. pmarks_1Chr.json confirms the petuchah after 28:21, which the row correctly flags single-witness and non-driving. What nobody has checked against the text is one comparison sentence the repair imported wholesale.

challenges.claim: The row asserts that 22:13's חֲזַ֣ק וֶאֱמָ֔ץ אַל תִּירָ֖א וְאַל תֵּחָֽת 'matches 28:20's continuation word for word'. It does not. That continuation reads חֲזַ֤ק וֶאֱמַץ֙ וַעֲשֵׂ֔ה אַל תִּירָ֖א וְאַל תֵּחָ֑ת, interposing a third word between the imperative pair and the negated pair; aligned token by token on the consonantal skeleton the two diverge at position three (22:13 gives חזק / ואמץ / אל / תירא / ואל / תחת, six tokens, against seven at 28:20 with ועשה inserted after ואמץ). The second imperative differs in pointing and accent between the two verses as well (וֶאֱמָ֔ץ at 22:13 against וֶאֱמַץ֙ at 28:20), as do תֵּחָֽת and תֵּחָ֑ת. The overstatement is self-defeating in context: the very word that breaks the alignment, וַעֲשֵׂ֔ה, is the one the row names two clauses later as 28:20's unique point of contact with 28:10, so the sentence claims an identity that its own conclusion needs to be false. The phrase was inherited verbatim from the upheld challenge, but the revised row now asserts it in its own voice.
challenges.suggested_action: State the relation as the text supports it — 22:13 supplies the same imperative pair and the same negated pair, which 28:20 reproduces with the do-imperative wedged between them — so that the repertoire point and the shared-element point stop contradicting one another.

primary_reviews.rationale: Two universal-shaped claims here, both tested programmatically and both true. 'Without any inquit ever reopening the address': a sweep of אמר over 28:1-29:22 finds forms only at 29:1, 29:10 and 29:20 in this stretch — none anywhere in 29:11-19 — so the prayer is indeed one uninterrupted utterance between its frame at וַיְבָ֤רֶךְ דָּוִיד֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל הַקָּהָ֑ל and the outward turn at וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִיד֙ לְכָל הַקָּהָ֔ל בָּֽרְכוּ. 'Returns to the very project that opened this part': בירה occurs in the whole of 1Chr at exactly two places, הַבִּירָ֔ה at 29:1 and וְלִבְנ֖וֹת הַבִּירָ֥ה אֲשֶׁר הֲכִינֽוֹתִי at 29:19, so the return is real and demonstrable rather than impressionistic. The rejected alternative also checks out — v13's וְעַתָּ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ pivot brings no change of addressee, the second-person reference to God continuing unbroken through לָ֑ךְ — so declining to break there is right. PE at 1Chr.29.19 is correctly typed, disclosed, and undoubled; all seven quotes collated exact. One fidelity caveat below challenge threshold: the gloss attached to the 29:10 slice reads '..., and said', but וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דָּוִ֗יד sits outside the quoted string, which stops at the atnach; the same string is glossed without that overhang elsewhere in this cluster.

The blessing-inquit at v10 correctly opens a single uninterrupted second-person address to Yahweh that runs through the patriarchal invocation of v18 to the petition for Solomon in v19, and v20's turn to a fresh congregation-directed inquit is the right close. But the claim that v19 'closes by returning to the very project that opened this part' misplaces its own inclusio: הַבִּירָה (the palace/citadel) first opens at 29:1 -- inside the preceding decision (143), not inside this row's own span -- so the phrase misattributes where the bracket actually begins, and the rejected-alternative field never engages the stronger rival this raises.

primary_reviews.rationale: Collation on this row is clean. Its five contiguous Hebrew runs -- 29:20, 29:22, the two segments flanking the 29:25 ellipsis, and 29:26 -- each match 1Chr_oshb.txt byte for byte and each resolves to the verse the row assigns it, with no stray hits elsewhere in the book. The morphology carrying the opening argument holds: בָּֽרְכוּ is a plural imperative and the 2mp suffix on אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם fixes the assembly as the addressed party, so the row is right that v20 issues direction rather than reporting sentiment. One precision the row could have used in its own favour: the imperative is enacted first by its cognate, וַיְבָרֲכ֣וּ כָֽל הַקָּהָ֗ל, and only afterwards by the bowing and prostrating it names. Two book-wide sweeps corroborate rather than damage the row -- שֵׁנִית֙ occurs exactly once in all of 1 Chronicles, here at 29:22 (וַיַּמְלִ֤יכוּ שֵׁנִית֙), so calling this a pointedly marked repeat enthronement is not overstated, and the first enthronement it counts from sits in-book at 23:1 (וַיַּמְלֵ֛ךְ אֶת שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בְנ֖וֹ עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל), so the claim needs no cross-book crutch. The crosswalk lists chapter 29 as identical (30 WEB, 30 MT) and it falls outside every offset zone, so the row's parallel web:/oshb: numbering is correct and no dual cite is owed. The pe cited after 29:19 is real and correctly typed in pmarks_1Chr.json. What I cannot pass is how the argument is distributed: the row spends its case defending the one edge the shared strategy affirms, misnames that edge as the strategy's flagged uncertainty, mentions without arguing the join the strategy actually flags, and meets the rival on pragmatic ground while leaving the rival's lexical support untouched. I note separately, without raising it as a challenge because marks never drive a boundary, an internal inconsistency in this cluster's tier-3 disclosure: the pe standing after 29:25 at this row's own closing edge is absent from its ref list although the adjoining row cites that same mark, and the 29:19 pe appears in the refs with no disclosing sentence anywhere in the prose.

challenges.claim: The span absorbs the one join the shared strategy pre-flags, and the Hebrew supplies a tier-1 driver exactly there. §7 item 15 reads "29:21-25 enthronement notice (close of assembly vs its own unit)", so the flagged seam is 29:20|29:21, interior to this row. At that seam the text changes calendar day: 29:21 opens וַיִּזְבְּח֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה זְ֠בָחִים וַיַּעֲל֨וּ עֹל֜וֹת לַיהוָ֗ה לְֽמָחֳרַת֮ הַיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֒ ("they sacrificed sacrifices to Yahweh and offered burnt offerings to Yahweh on the morrow of that day"), where לְֽמָחֳרַת֮ הַיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֒ is an explicit temporal displacement, and 29:22 then anchors itself to the new day with בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא. A stated change of day is a tier-1 scene/time signal on the contract's own list, not a marker claim. The row's entire treatment of it is the appositive "the next-day sacrifice (29:21)": the seam is named and never reasoned, which is precisely the condition §8 instructs primaries to challenge ("challenge any span hiding an unargued internal tier-1 seam").
challenges.suggested_action: Argue 29:20|29:21 on its merits -- for instance that the morrow-clause continues one liturgical occasion under a single unbroken assembly rather than opening a new scene -- or split the row there. Either outcome is acceptable; leaving the flagged seam unreasoned is not.

challenges.claim: The row's stated reason for holding medium confidence rests on a strategy flag that does not exist at the edge claimed. It reports the low-confidence question as "whether v20 belongs with the prayer that precedes it as the congregation's response, or opens its own unit", but §7's only 1 Chronicles 29 entry is item 15, which localises the doubt at the enthronement notice 29:21-25, and §6's block map affirmatively lists "29:10-19 David's blessing-prayer; 29:20-25 worship + Solomon enthroned". The strategy therefore endorses the 29:19|29:20 edge and reserves its doubt for the interior join. On the evidence that edge is in fact the better supported of the two: a fresh wayyiqtol speech frame, וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִיד֙ לְכָל הַקָּהָ֔ל, which is tier-1, with a petuchah after 29:19 agreeing but not driving (single-witness).
challenges.suggested_action: Correct the attribution to §7 item 15. If medium confidence is retained, anchor it in the unargued 29:20|29:21 seam that the strategy actually flags, rather than in the 29:19|29:20 edge the block map supports.

challenges.claim: The rejected alternative is defeated only in its weakest form. The row's counter -- that v20 issues a new imperative rather than reporting a reaction -- is true as far as it goes. But the strongest version of the rival is lexical, not pragmatic. A sweep of the ברך root across chapter 29 returns exactly two verses, 29:10 and 29:20, with nothing between or after them. 29:10 reads וַיְבָ֤רֶךְ דָּוִיד֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל הַקָּהָ֑ל ("David blessed Yahweh in the sight of all the assembly"); 29:20 pairs בָּֽרְכוּ נָ֖א with וַיְבָרֲכ֣וּ כָֽל הַקָּהָ֗ל. The same three elements -- the ברך root, דָּוִיד֙, and כָּל הַקָּהָ֑ל -- stand at both ends and at no other point in the chapter. That is an inclusio/refrain pattern, tier-1 on the contract's list, and it is the rival's real support: it can be read as closing 29:10-20 rather than opening a unit at v20. The row never engages it, so what it rejected is not the strongest rival available.
challenges.suggested_action: Engage the 29:10 / 29:20 envelope of ברך plus כָּל הַקָּהָ֑ל directly, and state why it functions as a resumptive re-head opening a new movement rather than as a closing inclusio. The imperative-versus-report observation does not by itself decide between those two readings.

challenges.claim: The 29:25 citation is grammatically decapitated by its own ellipsis, and its gloss drops a restriction the Hebrew states. Both quoted segments are byte-exact, but the elided material is לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּתֵּ֤ן עָלָיו֙ ה֣וֹד מַלְכ֔וּת, which contains ה֣וֹד מַלְכ֔וּת -- the very antecedent the relative אֲ֠שֶׁר modifies. As quoted, the relative clause is presented with no head inside the quotation. The quote also stops at לְפָנָ֖יו while the verse continues עַל כָּל מֶ֛לֶךְ לְפָנָ֖יו עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, and the row's gloss ("such as had not been on any king before him") omits עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, so the incomparability reads as absolute where the Hebrew limits it to kings over Israel. challenges.claim: The new 29:20|29:21 argument stands on two legs, and the second reverses under the row's own principle. It writes that '29:22 explicitly anchors itself back to that same occasion, בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא'. But 29:21 has just displaced the action to לְֽמָחֳרַת֮ הַיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֒, the morrow of v20's day, and 29:22 opens with וַיֹּאכְל֨וּ וַיִּשְׁתּ֜וּ, continuing v21's wayyiqtol chain (וַיִּזְבְּח֣וּ ... וַיַּעֲל֨וּ) with no temporal reset and no change of subject. On precisely the principle invoked one clause earlier — that an unbroken wayyiqtol chain under one subject holds the narration to a single occasion — the eating and drinking belong to the day of the sacrificing, namely the morrow; so the demonstrative at v22 points at the newly introduced day rather than back across the shift, corroborating the displacement instead of dissolving it. The translation reads that join the same way, running v22 on as a continuation of v21's sentence ('...in abundance for all Israel, and ate and drank before Yahweh on that day'). At best the phrase is anaphorically ambiguous between the morrow and the הַיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֒ embedded inside v21's own construct, so 'explicitly' cannot be sustained on either reading.
challenges.suggested_action: Drop this leg or invert it. The first leg carries the join unaided, since v21's implied 3mp subject continues the assembly that performed וַיְבָרֲכ֣וּ, וַיִּקְּד֧וּ and וַיִּֽשְׁתַּחֲו֛וּ at v20 with no fresh inquit or addressee intervening. Alternatively, concede that the v22 demonstrative most naturally denotes the morrow, then argue that a stated day-change unaccompanied by any change of speaker, audience or participant set does not by itself open a unit here. What cannot stand is citing v22 as an explicit anchor back to the day of v20.

peer_crosscheck.assessment: Five challenges land on this row and all five hold up on independent verification, though one (LF-145-1) needs a particular corrected. book_strategy_draft.md §6 item 15 reads exactly "29:21-25 enthronement notice (close of assembly vs its own unit)" and §6's block map lists "29:10-19 David's blessing-prayer; 29:20-25 worship + Solomon enthroned" as settled, not disputed -- so the row's stated confidence driver ("whether v20 belongs with the prayer that precedes it... or opens its own unit") cites a dispute at an edge the strategy does not flag (OL-145-2, supported). The seam §7.15 actually names sits inside the row's own span, at v21's וַיִּזְבְּח֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה זְ֠בָחִים וַיַּעֲל֨וּ עֹל֜וֹת לַיהוָ֗ה לְֽמָחֳרַת֮ הַיּ֣וֹם הַהוּא֒ פָּרִ֨ים אֶ֜לֶף אֵילִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף כְּבָשִׂ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף וְנִסְכֵּיהֶ֑ם וּזְבָחִ֥ים לָרֹ֖ב לְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל ("on the morrow of that day"), which the rationale names only in passing ("the next-day sacrifice (29:21)") and never argues for or against -- confirmed as an unargued internal tier-1-type seam per §8's own instruction to primaries (OL-145-1, HIGH, supported). LF-145-1 reaches the same core conclusion independently, but its own Hebrew for this clause does not byte-collate against 1Chr_oshb.txt, and its parallel claim that v23's subject-narrowing to Solomon (וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב שְׁ֠לֹמֹה עַל כִּסֵּ֨א יְהוָ֧ה לְמֶ֛לֶךְ תַּֽחַת דָּוִ֥יד אָבִ֖יו וַיַּצְלַ֑ח וַיִּשְׁמְע֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל) is "exactly the type" §2's gathering-verb bullet names overstates the match -- that bullet's own listed examples (11:1, 28:1, both gathering/convening verbs) are a different class from v23's sat-down verb. The correction is supplied below; the core point that the row leaves §7.15's seam unargued still stands and is independently confirmed by OL-145-1 (ruled supported_with_correction). Beyond the seam question, the rejected_alternative meets only the pragmatic form of the rival reading (imperative vs. report) and leaves the lexical form untouched: a consonantal sweep of ch.29 confirms the brk root occurs in exactly two verses, 10 and 20, framing a real inclusio/refrain candidate the row never engages (OL-145-3, supported). primary_reviews.rationale: Every load-bearing element of this row survives inspection. Its four Hebrew citations (29:26, 29:27, 29:29, 29:30) are byte-exact against 1Chr_oshb.txt, and the row reproduced the WLC's defectively pointed וְהָאֲחרֹנִ֑ים -- het carrying no vowel -- rather than silently normalising it, which is the right instinct for a single-witness source. The syntactic characterisation of the opening is accurate: 29:26 is waw plus fronted proper-noun subject plus qatal, breaking the unbroken wayyiqtol chain that runs through 29:20-25, and it carries neither addressee nor scene-verb as claimed. The reign arithmetic the row leans on is internally consistent inside the single verse: 29:27's שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים at Hebron plus שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וְשָׁלֽוֹשׁ at Jerusalem total the אַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה that same verse states (7 + 33 = 40), so no external figure is imported. Both mark claims verify against pmarks_1Chr.json: 1Chr.29.25 = PE and 1Chr.29.30 = PE, neither doubled, both correctly flagged single-witness, and the row's own sentence that the two breaks merely agree with edges they do not cause is exactly the tier-3 posture the contract demands. The terminal claim is true rather than rhetorical: 1Chr.29.30 is the last of the source's 943 verse lines and chapter 29 closes at v30, so there genuinely is no following verse against which a closing edge could be tested. Chapter 29 is crosswalked as identical, so the matched web:/oshb: numbering owes no dual cite, and the ref list covers every verse from which Hebrew is quoted. My two objections are descriptive rather than structural -- a formula named that the cited verse does not contain, and a gloss that erases a title distinction internal to the very form the row identifies. Neither disturbs the span, and I would expect both to be answerable by rewording.

challenges.claim: The opening edge is described by a formula absent from the verse it is said to echo. The row states that its opening clause "echoes the very throne-formula the previous row just closed on". The previous row closes on 29:25, and a sweep of כסא across chapter 29 returns a single verse -- 29:23, וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב שְׁ֠לֹמֹה עַל כִּסֵּ֨א יְהוָ֧ה -- so there is no throne lexeme in 29:25 at all; the throne clause sits two verses earlier and is not what the prior row closed on. The echo the row reaches for is real but lies elsewhere: 29:25 ends עַל כָּל מֶ֛לֶךְ לְפָנָ֖יו עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל and 29:26 reads מָלַ֖ךְ עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, so what actually recurs is the מלך field (noun מֶ֛לֶךְ answered by finite מָלַ֖ךְ) together with the עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל tail. Because the opening-edge characterisation is built on this echo, mislabelling the echoed material weakens the warrant as stated.
challenges.suggested_action: Rename the echoed element: מֶ֛לֶךְ at 29:25 answered by מָלַ֖ךְ plus עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל at 29:26, rather than "throne-formula", which belongs to 29:23 and sits inside the preceding row rather than at its closing edge.

challenges.claim: The colophon gloss flattens a lexical distinction constitutive of the form the row is naming. 29:29 titles its three sources with three different nouns -- שְׁמוּאֵ֣ל הָרֹאֶ֔ה, נָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֔יא, and גָּ֥ד הַחֹזֶֽה -- but the row's rendering gives "Samuel the seer, Nathan the prophet, and Gad the seer", collapsing הָרֹאֶ֔ה and הַחֹזֶֽה into one English word. The threefold title variation is part of what makes this a source-citation colophon, so the evidence as presented understates the very feature supporting the literature_type_guess. The gloss additionally compresses the three repeated דִּבְרֵי֙ constructs into a single "history of".
challenges.suggested_action: Distinguish the two terms in the gloss, rendering הָרֹאֶ֔ה and הַחֹזֶֽה separately, so the colophon's three-term title variation is visible in the evidence that supports the form call.

primary_reviews.rationale: This row lands on ground the book strategy pre-names as its own device (§2: "Source-citation colophon + regnal summary: 29:26-30"), and the closing edge is uncontestable on its own terms: v30 is the book's final verse, so there is no rival text to argue a further edge against. The internal join at v28/29 is well defended -- v29's וְדִבְרֵי דָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ הָרִאשֹׁנִים וְהָאֲחֹרֹנִים carries forward the just-totaled reign with no new scene-verb, so splitting the résumé (26-28) from the colophon (29-30) would genuinely cut one movement in two, as the rejected_alternative says. One line overstates the connection at the shared edge, though: it calls v26's opener an echo of 'the very throne-formula the previous row just closed on,' but the verse the prior row (145) actually closes on, v25, reads הֹוְדַ מַלְכוּת ('splendor of kingship') -- no כִּסֵּא ('throne') word at all. The actual throne-sitting formula, עַל כִּסֵּא יְהוָה, sits at v23, inside the prior row but three verses before its closing edge. What genuinely links v25 and v26 is the shared מלךְ root (הֹוְד מַלְכוּת / מָלַךְ), not a reproduced throne formula, and the boundary argument does not actually need the overstated claim to stand.

challenges.claim: The rationale states v26 'echoes the very throne-formula the previous row just closed on,' but the previous row (M8-1Chr-145) closes on v25, whose Hebrew (oshb 1Chr.29.25) is וַיִּתֵּן עָלָיוֹ הֹוְד מַלְכוּת ('gave him splendor of kingship') and contains no כִּסֵּא ('throne') word at all. The verse that actually contains a throne-sitting formula, וַיֵּשֶב שְׁלֹמֹה עַל כִּסֵּא יְהוָה (oshb 1Chr.29.23), sits inside 145's span but three verses before its actual closing edge, so it is not the verse being 'closed on.' The genuine link between v25 and v26 is the shared מלךְ root (מַלְכוּת / מָלַךְ), which is a narrower and different claim than a reproduced throne formula.
challenges.suggested_action: Replace 'echoes the very throne-formula the previous row just closed on' with an accurate characterization -- e.g., 'shares the מלךְ root with v25's הֹוְד מַלְכוּת' -- since the boundary argument (subject-first clause, no scene-verb, new regnal-résumé formula) does not depend on the throne-formula claim and stands without it.

primary_reviews.rationale: The mislabelled warrant is genuinely replaced rather than merely softened, and its substitute is verifiable: 29:25 does close עַל כָּל מֶ֛לֶךְ לְפָנָ֖יו עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, 29:26 does answer with מָלַ֖ךְ עַל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, and כסא occurs once in the chapter, at 29:23. The bracketing paragraphing is as reported, pmarks_1Chr.json keying PE to both 29:25 and 29:30, with each flagged single-witness and each denied any driving role; 1Chr_oshb.txt does terminate at 1Chr.29.30, so the remark that no later verse remains to argue a closing edge against is factually right. challenges.claim: 29:28 is the one verse across all six of this cluster's spans that has no entry of its own in its row's boundary_evidence_refs. peer_crosscheck.assessment: Three low-severity challenges, all supported, and the first two converge on one defect. The row's claim that v26 "echoes the very throne-formula the previous row just closed on" is inaccurate on its own terms: 145 closes on v25, whose Hebrew (וַיְגַדֵּ֨ל יְהוָ֤ה אֶת שְׁלֹמֹה֙ לְמַ֔עְלָה לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּתֵּ֤ן עָלָיו֙ ה֣וֹד מַלְכ֔וּת אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא הָיָ֧ה עַל כָּל מֶ֛לֶךְ לְפָנָ֖יו עַל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל) contains no throne lexeme at all; the throne-sitting formula, וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב שְׁ֠לֹמֹה עַל כִּסֵּ֨א יְהוָ֧ה לְמֶ֛לֶךְ, sits two verses earlier at v23, inside 145's span but not at its closing edge -- confirmed against 1Chr_oshb.txt. LF-146-1 and OL-146-1 make the identical correction independently, so one remedy serves both: the real recurring element is the mlk root (noun in v25 answered by the finite verb in v26), not a reproduced throne formula. The boundary argument itself -- subject-first clause, no scene-verb, new regnal-résumé formula -- does not depend on the overstated line and stands without it. The third challenge (OL-146-2) is a real if minor observation: the colophon's gloss renders both הָרֹאֶ֔ה and הַחֹזֶֽה as "seer," collapsing a lexical distinction between two of the three source-titles that is part of what makes the row's own literature_type_guess (source-citation colophon) legible in its cited evidence. Worth noting for the author round: this collapse reproduces WEB's own rendering at 29:29 verbatim (confirmed against 1Chr_web_clean.txt: WEB also gives "Samuel the seer... Gad the seer"), so it is not an invented gloss -- but the critique about evidentiary visibility of the threefold title variation still holds regardless of source. Span, closing-edge finality (v30 is the corpus's terminal line -- confirmed programmatically at 943 verse lines in 1Chr_oshb.txt), the reign arithmetic (7+33=40 in v27, internally consistent), and the two PE disclosures at 29:25/29:30 all check out clean. Nothing in this cluster's three items bears on span or confidence.
